question: The Commission is developing product-specific requirements under the Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation1, including a proposed ecodesign label providing information on environmental performance.

Concerns have been raised about the proposed Environmental Performance Class methodology, particularly the Product Environmental Footprint method, which may insufficiently account for substances of concern and favour certain materials. Broad product categories may also distort comparisons, potentially misleading consumers.
Furthermore, additional information requirements risk increasing administrative burdens without improving product sustainability. In this regard: 1.

How will the Commission ensure that delegated acts prioritise mandatory requirements directly improving product environmental performance, while ensuring that the Environmental Performance Class adequately accounts for substances of concern and avoids methodological biases between materials?
Given the Digital Product Passport, what added value does a physical label provide and would the Commission consider relying primarily on digital information?

If introduced, how will the Commission ensure that the physical label remains simple, avoids misleading consumers and ensures equal treatment of the EU ecolabel and other officially recognised ISO 14024 ecolabels, such as the Nordic Swan Ecolabel?

Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 June 2024 establishing a framework for the setting of ecodesign requirements for sustainable products, amending Directive (EU) 2020/1828 and Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 and repealing Directive 2009/125/EC, OJ L, 2024/1781, 28.6.2024, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1781/oj. 1
